# HomeContentsInsurance.co.nz

> New Zealand home contents insurance referral service connecting renters, homeowners, and landlords with NZ-licensed insurance advisers.

HomeContentsInsurance.co.nz is a lead generation and referral service operating in New Zealand. We connect consumers with NZ-licensed financial advisers who specialise in home contents insurance. Advisers referred through this service hold a Financial Advice Provider (FAP) licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (FMCA). The referral service is free to consumers; advisers earn commission from insurers.

## What We Cover

- Renters / tenant contents insurance — cover for your belongings when renting
- Homeowner contents insurance — cover for household items in an owned home
- Landlord contents insurance — cover for landlord-owned furnishings in rental properties
- High-value / specified items insurance — jewellery, art, watches, collections
- Portable valuables cover — items taken outside the home (phones, cameras, laptops)
- Accidental damage contents insurance — breakage and accidental damage cover
- Temporary accommodation / loss of use — alternative accommodation after a covered event

## About This Service

HomeContentsInsurance.co.nz is not an insurer or licensed financial adviser. We are a lead generation and referral service. All advisers referred through this service are independently licensed under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. Adviser fees are funded by insurer commission; there is no cost to the consumer.

## NZ Market Context

New Zealand's home contents insurance market is dominated by a small number of major providers: AA Insurance, AMI (IAG), State (IAG), Tower Insurance, Vero, and Chubb Life. Contents insurance in NZ typically covers theft, fire, water damage, accidental damage (optional), and EQC natural hazard events. EQC (Earthquake Commission) provides a base layer of natural hazard cover (up to NZ$300,000 for contents since 2024), with private insurer cover applying above that threshold.

Key regulatory context:
- Financial advisers providing personalised advice must hold a FAP licence under the FMCA 2013
- EQC Act 2022 revised natural hazard cover effective 1 October 2022
- Insurance Contract Law reform under review by MBIE as of 2025
